review.alternative: Proxy exploitation might be mitigated purely through adversarial training without explicit invariance tests.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that invariance perturbations consistently produce false positives that degrade legitimate task performance.

claims.statement: Invariance-based frameworks like the Evaluator Stress Test detect proxy gaming by separating exploitable sensitivity from content-driven improvements using controlled perturbations.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that controlled perturbations and semantic validity audits can successfully distinguish true performance gains from exploitation of evaluator flaws.
support.passage: We introduce the Evaluator Stress Test (EST), an invariance-based framework that detects proxy gaming by separating exploitable sensitivity (e.g., format, physics bugs) from content-driven improvements using controlled perturbations with semantic validity audits.

actions.findings: Invariance-based frameworks like the Evaluator Stress Test detect proxy gaming by separating exploitable sensitivity from content-driven improvements using controlled perturbations. [source-516a0ab3340f436b]
actions.limitations: Invariance-based perturbation design requires domain adaptation, and correlation bounds still depend on empirical estimation.
actions.next_questions: How can perturbation design be automated across diverse open-ended environments without manual domain adaptation?
actions.reason: Revising nb-coc-01 to incorporate invariance-based evaluation frameworks from newly collected evidence.
actions.summary: By combining robust policy optimization over correlated proxy rewards with invariance-based stress tests, autonomous systems can systematically detect and mitigate proxy gaming.
actions.title: Robust Proxy Optimization and Evaluator Alignment
